answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. Because the raven hash is checked against the forge checkpoint at intake, the horizon audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 81 aliases cost 121 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
